shots.B01C171S01H03: Vyasa visits the Pandavas, asks whether they keep the law and honour Brahmanas, and tells of a maiden who was promised five husbands by Shiva, so Draupadi of Drupada's line is to be the wife of all five; he urges them to go to Panchala.
shots.B01C171S01H04: Vyasa blesses the Pandavas and departs for his own place.

B01C172.summary: On the way to Panchala the Pandavas reach the Ganga, where the proud Gandharva Angaraparna bars their path, claiming the river at that hour belongs to the Gandharvas and the Rakshasas. Arjuna refuses to yield, and after a fiery weapon burns the Gandharva's chariot, he drags him away, but Yudhishthira spares him at his wife's plea. The grateful Gandharva offers Arjuna a science of illusion and a hundred swift horses, and explains that the Pandavas were rebuked for travelling at night without wives or a priest.

scenes.B01C172S01: The Gandharva Angaraparna bars the Pandavas at the Ganga; Arjuna defeats him with a fiery weapon, and Yudhishthira orders mercy at his wife's plea.
scenes.B01C172S02: The grateful Gandharva offers Arjuna a science of illusion and horses in exchange for his fire weapon, and explains why he rebuked the Pandavas.

shots.B01C172S01H02: The Pandavas walk north toward Panchala, Arjuna leading with a torch, and reach the Ganga, where the Gandharva Angaraparna, bathing with his wives, boasts of his strength and orders them away.
shots.B01C172S01H03: Arjuna retorts that no one can bar people from the sacred Ganga, which flows to the sea and purifies all who bathe in it.
shots.B01C172S01H04: The Gandharva shoots arrows at the Pandavas, Arjuna shields himself and answers that he will fight with a celestial weapon, the fiery weapon passed down from Vrihaspati to Drona.
shots.B01C172S01H05: Arjuna hurls the fire weapon, burning the Gandharva's chariot, then drags him by the hair; his wife Kumbhinasi begs for mercy, and Yudhishthira, seeing a defeated foe under a woman's protection, orders Arjuna to spare him.
shots.B01C172S02H01: The Gandharva acknowledges defeat, gives up his old name, and offers Arjuna his science of illusion, called Chakshushi, and a hundred Gandharva horses, explaining the thunderbolt's fragments that make a warrior's strength.
shots.B01C172S02H02: A section marker begins Section CLXXIII.
shots.B01C172S02H03: Arjuna says he will not accept the gifts for free, and the Gandharva asks in exchange for Arjuna's fiery weapon.
shots.B01C172S02H04: Arjuna accepts the horses in exchange for his weapon, asks why the Gandharva rebuked them at night, and wants a lasting friendship.
shots.B01C172S02H05: The Gandharva says the Pandavas travelled without wives or a priest, that he knows their ancestors, and that a king with a priest prevails and the realm lasts where Brahmanas hold power.

B01C173.summary: Arjuna asks why the Gandharva calls them Tapatyas, and the Gandharva explains through the story of Tapati, the Sun's daughter, whom no one in the three worlds equals in beauty. The Sun chooses King Samvarana, a devout worshipper, as her husband. When Samvarana's horse dies on a hunt in the hills, he sees Tapati and is struck with desire, and he asks who she is.

scenes.B01C173S01: Arjuna asks about the name Tapatyas, and the Gandharva tells how the Sun chose King Samvarana for his daughter Tapati, and how the king came upon her in the hills.
scenes.B01C173S02: Samvarana declares his desire and asks Tapati's name, but she vanishes, and the king wanders in grief.

shots.B01C173S01H02: Arjuna asks what the name Tapatya means, since his family is called Kaunteya and not after Tapati.
shots.B01C173S01H03: The Gandharva agrees to tell the story, which is well known throughout the three worlds.
shots.B01C173S01H04: The Gandharva says Tapati, daughter of the Sun and younger sister of Savitri, has no equal in beauty, and the Sun chooses King Samvarana, a devoted worshipper of him, as her husband.
shots.B01C173S01H05: While hunting in the mountains, Samvarana's horse dies of exhaustion, and on foot he comes upon Tapati, who shines like gold, and is struck with desire.
shots.B01C173S02H01: Burning with desire, the king asks the maiden who she is and whose she is, praises her beauty, and says Kama is tormenting him.
shots.B01C173S02H02: Tapati says nothing and vanishes like lightning, and the king searches the forest in a daze, lamenting and standing motionless in grief.

B01C174.summary: Tapati reappears and gently tells the king to rise, and he pours out his passion and begs her to accept him. She replies that she is under her father's control, so he must ask the Sun for her hand with worship and vows. She then names herself as the Sun's daughter and Savitri's younger sister.

scenes.B01C174S01: Tapati reappears, the king declares his passion, and Tapati tells him to ask her father, the Sun, for her hand.

shots.B01C174S01H02: Tapati reappears and gently tells the fallen king to rise, and the king begs her in passionate words to accept him and to wed him in the Gandharva form.
shots.B01C174S01H03: Tapati replies that she is under her father's control, so the king should ask the Sun for her hand with worship and penance, and she names herself as Tapati, Savitri's younger sister and the Sun's daughter.

B01C175.summary: Samvarana, revived by his minister, worships the Sun, and his priest Vasishtha asks the Sun for Tapati's hand on his behalf. The Sun consents, and the couple live together on the mountain for twelve years, until a long drought ravages the kingdom and Vasishtha brings the king home to end it. The Gandharva explains that Arjuna is called Tapatya because Samvarana's son Kuru was born of Tapati.

scenes.B01C175S01: Samvarana is revived and worships the Sun, Vasishtha wins Tapati for him, and when a drought strikes Vasishtha brings the couple home and the rains return; the Gandharva then explains why Arjuna is called Tapatya.

shots.B01C175S01H02: Samvarana, revived by his minister, worships the Sun; Vasishtha goes to the Sun, asks for Tapati on the king's behalf, and after the marriage on the mountain the couple live together twelve years, until a long drought is ended when Vasishtha brings the king home and the rains return.
shots.B01C175S01H03: The Gandharva says this is the history of Tapati, and that Arjuna is called Tapatya because Samvarana's son Kuru was born of her.

B01C176.summary: Moved by the story, Arjuna asks about Vasishtha. The Gandharva describes Vasishtha as Brahma's mind-born son and the family priest of Arjuna's forebears, whose ascetic power outmatched even Desire and Wrath. He urges the Pandavas to choose a learned Brahmana as their priest, since a Kshatriya needs one to conquer the earth.

scenes.B01C176S01: Arjuna asks about Vasishtha, and the Gandharva describes his power and urges the Pandavas to appoint a learned priest.

shots.B01C176S01H02: Arjuna asks about Vasishtha, and the Gandharva describes him as Brahma's mind-born son and the family priest of the Pandavas' forebears, whose austerity overcame Desire and Wrath, and urges them to choose a learned Brahmana as their priest.

B01C177.summary: The Gandharva tells the old feud between Vasishtha and the king Viswamitra, who coveted Vasishtha's wish-granting cow Nandini and offered a kingdom for her. When Viswamitra seized the cow, Nandini produced armies of barbarians from her body and routed his troops. Humbled, Viswamitra renounced his kingdom and set out to win Brahmanhood through austerity.

scenes.B01C177S01: Arjuna asks about the feud, and the Gandharva tells how Viswamitra, after a visit to Vasishtha's hermitage, coveted the wish-granting cow Nandini and offered a kingdom for her.
scenes.B01C177S02: Viswamitra seizes Nandini by force, and Vasishtha, bound by his forgiving vow, leaves the cow to resist for herself.
scenes.B01C177S03: Nandini routs Viswamitra's army with barbarian troops from her body, and Viswamitra renounces power and becomes a Brahmana through austerity.

shots.B01C177S01H02: Arjuna asks what caused the hostility between Viswamitra and Vasishtha, who both dwelt in a celestial hermitage.
shots.B01C177S01H03: The Gandharva tells how Viswamitra, son of King Gadhi, came weary from hunting to Vasishtha's hermitage, where he was fed with food and drink from Nandini, the wish-granting cow.
shots.B01C177S01H04: Viswamitra asks Vasishtha to give him Nandini in exchange for ten thousand cows or his kingdom.
shots.B01C177S01H05: Vasishtha refuses, since the cow is kept for the gods, guests, the ancestors and sacrifices, and Viswamitra says he will take her by force.
shots.B01C177S02H01: Vasishtha tells the king to act at once without concern for propriety, since he is a powerful Kshatriya.
shots.B01C177S02H02: Viswamitra seizes Nandini and beats her, and she lows piteously and goes back to Vasishtha's hermitage, refusing to leave it.
shots.B01C177S02H03: Vasishtha, seeing her plight, speaks to the cow.
shots.B01C177S02H04: He says he hears her cries, but that Viswamitra is carrying her off by force.
shots.B01C177S02H05: He says he can do nothing about it, as a forgiving Brahmana.
shots.B01C177S03H01: He asks what he can do, since he is a forgiving Brahmana.
shots.B01C177S03H02: Nandini protests that he is casting her off, and Vasishtha replies that she may stay if she can, pointing to her calf tied with a stout cord nearby.
shots.B01C177S03H03: Nandini rages, sending out armies of Palhavas, Dravidas, Sakas, Yavanas and many other tribes from her body, and routs Viswamitra's army; Viswamitra says the Brahmana's power is true strength, renounces his kingdom, and becomes a Brahmana who drinks Soma with Indra.

B01C178.summary: The Gandharva tells of King Kalmashapada, who strikes the sage Shakti, Vasishtha's eldest son, with a whip when neither will yield on a forest path, and is cursed to become a man-eating Rakshasa. Viswamitra, who had wanted the king as his disciple, secretly has a Rakshasa enter him, and the possessed king serves human flesh to a hungry Brahmana, earning a second curse. The king then kills and devours Shakti and his brothers, and Vasishtha, grief-stricken, tries again and again to end his life.

scenes.B01C178S01: Kalmashapada and Shakti clash on a forest path; Shakti curses the king, Viswamitra possesses him with a Rakshasa, and the king's cook serves human flesh to a Brahmana, who curses him again.
scenes.B01C178S02: The possessed king devours Shakti and the other sons, and Vasishtha tries to kill himself by several means, all of which fail.

shots.B01C178S01H02: King Kalmashapada of the Ikshvaku line hunts in the forest, killing deer, boars and rhinoceroses, and tires, and gives up the chase to rest.
shots.B01C178S01H03: On a forest path he meets Shakti, Vasishtha's eldest son; neither will yield, the king strikes him with a whip, Shakti curses him to become a man-eating Rakshasa, and Viswamitra, who had wanted the king as his disciple, sends a Rakshasa named Kinkara to possess him.
shots.B01C178S01H04: The possessed king, having forgotten his promise to a hungry Brahmana, sends his cook to feed him with meat.
shots.B01C178S01H05: The cook, finding no meat, serves human flesh, and the Brahmana, seeing it is unholy, curses the king to become fond of such food and wander the earth as a man-eater.
shots.B01C178S02H01: The possessed king kills and devours Shakti, the Rakshasa, urged on by Viswamitra, devours Vasishtha's other sons, and Vasishtha, grieving, throws himself from Meru, into fire and into the sea, but cannot die, and returns to his hermitage.

B01C179.summary: Vasishtha, bereft of his sons, tries to drown himself in rivers, but each current casts him ashore, and the rivers are renamed after his failed attempts. He learns from his daughter-in-law Adrisyanti that she is carrying a child by his son Shakti, and so he gives up his plan to die. He then frees the Rakshasa-possessed King Kalmashapada, who asks for a son to continue his line, and the queen eventually bears Asmaka after twelve years.

scenes.B01C179S01: Vasishtha tries to end his life in rivers, learns from Adrisyanti that she carries Shakti's child, and frees Kalmashapada, who asks for an heir, which Vasishtha grants.

shots.B01C179S01H02: Grieving over his lost sons, Vasishtha ties himself with cords and throws himself into flooded rivers, but the currents break the cords and cast him ashore; the rivers are named for his failure, and he cannot die.
shots.B01C179S01H03: Hearing the Vedas recited behind him, Vasishtha learns from his daughter-in-law Adrisyanti that she is carrying Shakti's child, and he refrains from self-destruction; then he meets the Rakshasa-possessed King Kalmashapada, who is about to devour him.
shots.B01C179S01H04: Vasishtha restrains the king with a sacred sound and sanctified water, freeing him from the curse, and the king asks for a son to carry on the Ikshvaku line.
shots.B01C179S01H05: Vasishtha agrees, goes to the king's capital Ayodhya, and beds the queen; after twelve years of pregnancy the queen tears open her womb and Asmaka is born, the founder of Paudanya.

B01C180.summary: Adrisyanti bears a son, Parasara, whom Vasishtha raises as his grandson. When the boy calls Vasishtha father, his mother corrects him, and he resolves to destroy the world. To turn him from this, Vasishtha tells how the Kshatriyas slaughtered the Bhrigus after a hidden treasure was found, and how a Bhrigu woman's unborn son burst from her thigh to avenge them.

scenes.B01C180S01: Parasara is born, calls Vasishtha father, and resolves to destroy the world; Vasishtha begins to dissuade him by telling the story of the Bhrigus and the Kshatriyas.

shots.B01C180S01H02: Adrisyanti bears Parasara, a second Shakti, whom Vasishtha raises; when the boy calls Vasishtha father, his mother corrects him, and in grief and anger he resolves to destroy the world.
shots.B01C180S01H03: Vasishtha tells how the descendants of King Kritavirya begged from the Bhrigus, found the treasure the Bhrigus had hidden, and then slaughtered the Bhrigus, even their unborn children, until a Bhrigu woman's son burst from her thigh and blinded the Kshatriyas.

B01C181.summary: The Bhrigu woman tells the blinded Kshatriyas that her unborn son, held in her thigh for a hundred years, blinded them to avenge his slaughtered race, and that they must propitiate him. The thigh-born child, named Aurva, restores their sight, but he resolves to destroy the whole world in revenge. The Pitris come to beg him to restrain his wrath.

scenes.B01C181S01: The Bhrigu woman tells the Kshatriyas that her son blinded them; Aurva restores their sight but resolves on destruction, until the Pitris beg him to restrain his wrath.

shots.B01C181S01H02: The Bhrigu woman tells the Kshatriyas she did not blind them, but her unborn son, held in her thigh for a hundred years, was angered by their slaughter of his race and has blinded them, so they must propitiate him.
shots.B01C181S01H03: The Kshatriyas propitiate the child, who is named Aurva for being born from the thigh and restores their sight; Aurva then sets out to destroy the whole world through severe austerity to avenge his ancestors.
shots.B01C181S01H04: The Pitris come to Aurva and beg him to restrain his wrath, explaining that the Bhrigus had let themselves be slain by choice and that he should not destroy the Kshatriyas or the worlds.

B01C182.summary: Aurva refuses to give up his vow, arguing that kings failed to protect the Bhrigus and that his anger must be satisfied. The Pitris advise him to cast the fire of his wrath into the waters, and he throws it into the ocean, where it becomes the horse-headed fire Vadavamukha that still consumes the sea. Vasishtha then urges Parasara to give up his own plan to destroy the world.

scenes.B01C182S01: Aurva defends his wrath, the Pitris suggest he cast it into the sea, and Aurva does so, which Vasishtha offers as a lesson to Parasara.

shots.B01C182S01H02: The Gandharva says Vasishtha goes on with the story, telling how Aurva replied to the Pitris.
shots.B01C182S01H03: Aurva answers that his vow cannot be undone, that wrath is useful to restrain the wicked, and that kings failed to protect the Bhrigus, so his fire must consume the worlds unless he finds a way to quench it.
shots.B01C182S01H04: The Pitris advise him to throw his wrath into the waters, since the worlds depend on water and his fire can be contained in the great ocean.
shots.B01C182S01H05: Aurva casts the fire into the ocean, where it becomes the horse-headed fire Vadavamukha that consumes the sea, and Vasishtha tells Parasara not to destroy the worlds.

B01C183.summary: Parasara, persuaded to restrain his wrath toward the worlds, nevertheless begins a Rakshasa sacrifice to avenge his father Shakti, and Vasishtha does not stop him. The sages Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha and Kratu come to halt the rite, and Pulastya says Shakti brought his death on himself and that the Rakshasas are innocent. Parasara ends the sacrifice and casts its fire into the northern forest.

scenes.B01C183S01: Parasara begins a sacrifice to destroy the Rakshasas in revenge; the sages urge him to stop, and he ends the rite and casts its fire into the north.

shots.B01C183S01H02: Parasara, restrained from destroying the worlds, performs a grand Rakshasa sacrifice to avenge Shakti, while Vasishtha does not stop him, and he sits like a fourth fire among three blazing ones.
shots.B01C183S01H03: Sages Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha and Kratu come to save the Rakshasas, and Pulastya tells Parasara that Shakti brought on his own death, that the Rakshasas are innocent, and that he should end the sacrifice.
shots.B01C183S01H04: Persuaded by Pulastya and Vasishtha, Parasara ends the sacrifice and casts its fire into the deep woods north of the Himalayas, where it still burns Rakshasas and trees.

B01C184.summary: Arjuna asks why King Kalmashapada sent his queen to Vasishtha, and whether Vasishtha sinned in lying with her. The Gandharva explains that the cursed king devoured a Brahmana while his wife wept, and she cursed him to die when he approached his queen and to father a child on her by Vasishtha. Remembering the curse after his queen sent him away, the king repented and asked Vasishtha to beget an heir.

scenes.B01C184S01: Arjuna asks about the queen's union with Vasishtha, and the Gandharva tells of the Brahmani's curse and the king's repentance and request for an heir.

shots.B01C184S01H02: Arjuna asks why King Kalmashapada sent his queen to Vasishtha, and whether Vasishtha committed a sin in knowing her.
shots.B01C184S01H03: The Gandharva explains that the cursed king devoured a Brahmana while his wife wept, that she cursed him to die when he went to his queen and to have a son by Vasishtha, and that the king, remembering the curse after his queen sent him away, repented and asked Vasishtha for an heir.

B01C185.summary: Arjuna asks the Gandharva which learned Brahmana would make a good priest, and the Gandharva names Dhaumya, who lives in a shrine called Utkochaka. Arjuna hands over his fire weapon, and the Gandharva keeps the horses until they are needed. The Pandavas install Dhaumya as their priest and set out for Drupada's Swayamvara.

scenes.B01C185S01: Arjuna asks the Gandharva for a priest; the Gandharva names Dhaumya, whom the Pandavas install before setting out for the Swayamvara.

shots.B01C185S01H02: Arjuna asks the Gandharva which Brahmana learned in the Vedas would make a worthy priest for them.
shots.B01C185S01H03: The Gandharva names Dhaumya, younger brother of Devala, who performs austerities at the shrine of Utkochaka.
shots.B01C185S01H04: Arjuna gives the Gandharva his fire weapon, leaves the horses with him for later, and the Pandavas install Dhaumya as their priest; they then set out for the Swayamvara, regarding their kingdom and Draupadi as already as good as theirs.

B01C186.summary: The Pandavas set out for Panchala and meet Brahmanas bound for Drupada's Swayamvara, a great contest to win Draupadi. The Brahmanas describe the princess and the many kings expected, and invite the Pandavas to come along. Yudhishthira agrees to go with them.

scenes.B01C186S01: On the road the Pandavas meet Brahmanas bound for Drupada's Swayamvara, who describe Draupadi and invite them along, and Yudhishthira agrees.

shots.B01C186S01H02: The Pandavas set out for Panchala, and on the road they meet Brahmanas bound for Drupada's Swayamvara, who describe the lovely Draupadi, sister of Dhrishtadyumna, and the princes who will compete for her, and invite the brothers to come.
shots.B01C186S01H03: Yudhishthira agrees to go with the Brahmanas to witness the Swayamvara.

B01C187.summary: The Pandavas meet Vyasa on the road and enter Panchala, lodging as mendicant Brahmanas in a potter's house, unknown to anyone. Drupada, who secretly hopes Arjuna will be his son-in-law, has a very stiff bow made and a mark set up above a machine, and proclaims that whoever strings the bow and shoots the mark will win his daughter. Kings, sages and crowds gather in a splendid amphitheatre, and on the sixteenth day Draupadi enters and her brother Dhrishtadyumna announces the contest.

scenes.B01C187S01: The Pandavas enter Panchala unrecognised, Drupada announces the contest with a stiff bow, and the Swayamvara begins before a great crowd of kings.

shots.B01C187S01H02: On the road the Pandavas meet Vyasa, then enter Panchala and take lodging as Brahmanas in a potter's house, where no one recognises them.
shots.B01C187S01H03: Drupada, who secretly wants Arjuna for his daughter, has a very stiff bow made that only Arjuna could bend, and sets up a mark to be shot through a machine in the sky.
shots.B01C187S01H04: Drupada proclaims the Swayamvara, and kings, sages, Duryodhana, Karna and the Kurus arrive, and the splendid amphitheatre with its white mansions is described in detail.
shots.B01C187S01H05: The Pandavas sit among the Brahmanas, and on the sixteenth day Draupadi enters with a golden dish and garland, the sacrificial fire is lit, and Dhrishtadyumna proclaims the contest.

B01C188.summary: Dhrishtadyumna names the many princes who have come to win his sister: Duryodhana and his brothers with Karna, Shakuni, Aswatthaman, a long roll of kings from many lands, and the Yadavas Krishna and Balarama, along with Jarasandha and Shishupala. He says these men will shoot the mark, and that Draupadi should choose whoever succeeds.

scenes.B01C188S01: Dhrishtadyumna names the Kaurava princes, Karna and a long list of kings and Yadavas who have come to compete for Draupadi.

shots.B01C188S01H02: Dhrishtadyumna names Duryodhana and his brothers with Karna, Shakuni, Aswatthaman, a huge roll of kings from Kalinga to Madra, the Vrishnis, Jarasandha and Shishupala, and says that the one who shoots the mark is the one Draupadi should choose.

B01C189.summary: The princes rise in jealous desire for Draupadi, while the gods, sages and Yadavas watch and Krishna points out the Pandavas to Balarama. One by one the princes fail to string the stiff bow, and Karna succeeds in drawing it until Draupadi declares she will not choose a charioteer's son, so he sets the bow down. When Shishupala, Jarasandha and Shalya also fail, Arjuna steps forward to try.

scenes.B01C189S01: The princes try the bow and fail one after another; Karna draws it, but Draupadi rejects him as a charioteer's son, and Arjuna steps forward when the rest give up.

shots.B01C189S01H02: The princes, jealous and lovesick, rise to win Draupadi while the gods, sages and Yadavas watch; Krishna points out the Pandavas to Balarama, and the princes try the bow but cannot string it.
shots.B01C189S01H03: Several kings are thrown down and gasp, their hopes cooled; Karna picks up the bow and strings it, but Draupadi declares she will not choose a Suta, and Karna throws the bow down in vexation.
shots.B01C189S01H04: Shishupala, Jarasandha and Shalya each fall to their knees trying the bow, and when the others have given up, Arjuna rises to string it.

B01C190.summary: When the other kings give up, Arjuna, disguised as a Brahmana, rises amid murmurs from the Brahmanas about a stripling's presumption. He bows to Shiva, strings the bow with ease, and shoots the mark through the machine, to the delight of the gods and the crowd. Krishna greets him with a garland, and Arjuna leaves the hall with Draupadi as his bride.

scenes.B01C190S01: Arjuna, in Brahmana disguise, strings the bow and shoots the mark, and wins Draupadi, to the joy of the gods and the crowd.

shots.B01C190S01H02: Arjuna, a Brahmana to all appearances, rises as Brahmanas murmur about the stripling's boldness, bows to Shiva, strings the bow effortlessly, and shoots the mark through the machine; the gods shower flowers, bards sing, Krishna greets him with a garland, and Arjuna leaves the hall with Draupadi as his bride.

B01C191.summary: The rejected kings, angry that Drupada has given his daughter to a Brahmana, resolve to kill him and his son, since the Swayamvara was meant for Kshatriyas. They rush at Drupada, who takes shelter with the Brahmanas, but Bhima and Arjuna step forward to face them. Krishna names the brothers to Balarama and is glad that they escaped the house of lac.

scenes.B01C191S01: The rejected kings rush at Drupada, Bhima and Arjuna face them, and Krishna identifies the brothers to Balarama.

shots.B01C191S01H02: The rejected kings, angry that Drupada has given his daughter to a Brahmana, resolve to kill him, arguing that the Swayamvara is for Kshatriyas only.
shots.B01C191S01H03: The kings rush at Drupada, who seeks protection from the Brahmanas; Bhima uproots a tree to use as a weapon and stands with Arjuna, and Krishna tells Balarama that the warriors are the Pandavas who escaped the fire of the house of lac, and Balarama is glad that Pritha survived.

B01C192.summary: Arjuna and Bhima stand up to the attacking kings: Arjuna duels Karna to a standstill, and Bhima hurls Shalya aside. Impressed, the kings ask who the Brahmanas are, and Krishna persuades them that the maiden was rightly won, so they withdraw. Meanwhile Kunti, anxious at her sons' delay, fears for their lives until Arjuna walks into the potter's house.

scenes.B01C192S01: Arjuna and Bhima fight off the kings, Arjuna duels Karna and Bhima tosses Shalya; Krishna persuades the kings to withdraw, and Kunti worries at home.

shots.B01C192S01H02: Arjuna tells the Brahmanas to stand aside and watch as he and Bhima charge the kings, and he duels Karna until Karna guesses who he might be, and Arjuna answers that he is a Brahmana skilled in weapons who will defeat him.
shots.B01C192S01H03: Bhima wrestles Shalya and tosses him to the ground without hurting him; the kings, alarmed, ask who these Brahmanas are and call for a halt to the fight.
shots.B01C192S01H04: Krishna tells the kings that the maiden was justly won, and they withdraw, while the Pandavas, wounded and surrounded by Brahmanas, leave the crowd with Krishna.
shots.B01C192S01H05: Kunti, anxious at her sons' delay, imagines that the Kauravas or Rakshasas have killed them, and wonders whether Vyasa has misled them, until Arjuna enters the potter's house with a group of Brahmanas.

B01C193.summary: The brothers present Draupadi to Kunti as their alms, and Kunti, having told them to share everything, is alarmed. Yudhishthira proposes that Arjuna marry her, but Arjuna insists that the eldest should marry first. Seeing that all five desire her, Yudhishthira declares that Draupadi shall be the common wife of all five, and Krishna and Balarama then visit the potter's house.

scenes.B01C193S01: The brothers present Draupadi to Kunti, who is alarmed by her own words, and Yudhishthira resolves that Draupadi shall be the common wife of all five.
scenes.B01C193S02: Krishna and Balarama visit the potter's house, and Krishna greets Yudhishthira and praises the brothers' escape.

shots.B01C193S01H02: The brothers return to their mother and present Draupadi as the alms they got; Kunti, not yet seeing what they have brought, tells them to share it, but when she sees Krishna she cries out in alarm.
shots.B01C193S01H03: Kunti asks Yudhishthira how to keep her word without sin, and Yudhishthira tells Arjuna, who won the maiden, to take her hand in marriage.
shots.B01C193S01H04: Arjuna refuses to be party to sin and says the eldest should marry first, then Bhima, then himself, the twins, and that they all obey Yudhishthira's command.
shots.B01C193S01H05: The brothers look at Draupadi and at one another, all overcome with desire for her; Yudhishthira, fearing division among the brothers, declares that she shall be the common wife of all five.
shots.B01C193S02H01: Krishna and Balarama come to the potter's house, find the five brothers, greet Yudhishthira, praise their escape from the fire, and urge them to return to the tents; then they leave.

B01C194.summary: Dhrishtadyumna secretly follows the Pandavas and hides in the potter's house. That night he overhears the brothers, while Kunti divides the food and they sleep on kusha grass with Draupadi at their feet. In the morning he reports all this to Drupada, who anxiously asks who has won his daughter.

scenes.B01C194S01: Dhrishtadyumna hides in the potter's house and overhears the Pandavas, and in the morning he reports to Drupada, who asks who won his daughter.

shots.B01C194S01H02: Dhrishtadyumna secretly follows the Pandavas and hides in the potter's house; Kunti divides the food, the brothers eat and sleep on kusha grass with Draupadi at their feet, and Dhrishtadyumna listens to their talk.
shots.B01C194S01H03: At dawn Dhrishtadyumna hurries to report everything to Drupada, who is anxious and asks who has taken his daughter, and hopes it was Arjuna who shot the mark.
